`PushResult` with `success=true` iff the push succeeded; otherwise\n    /// `success=false` with a human-readable reason. The `ref_name` field\n    /// contains the ref that was (or would have been) created.\n    pub fn push(config: &Config, sha: &str, run_id: &str) -> PushResult {\n        // Generate the epoch prefix: unix seconds (monotonic, time-derived).\n        // This is the GC lever (plan §4 \"RefPusher\").\n        let epoch = Self::epoch_now();\n\n        // Build the ref name based on push_mode\n        // Ref mode: refs/gantry/<epoch>-<sha> (default, recommended)\n        // Branch mode: refs/heads/gantry/<sha> (legacy, warns about mutation risk)\n        let ref_name = match &config.remote.push_mode {\n            PushMode::Ref => {\n                format!(\"refs/gantry/{epoch}-{sha}\")\n            }\n            PushMode::Branch => {\n                // Emit warning about mutation risk (S-1, INV-2)\n                eprintln!(\n                    \"[gantry] warning: push_mode=branch creates a mutable branch ref (refs/heads/gantry/{sha}).\",\n                );\n                eprintln!(\"[gantry] warning: this violates the 'no branch mutation' invariant and is a legacy escape hatch.\");\n                eprintln!(\"[gantry] warning: prefer push_mode=ref (hidden refs under refs/gantry/*) for production use.\");\n                format!(\"refs/heads/gantry/{sha}\")\n            }\n        };\n\n        // Run the push: git push <ci_remote> <sha>:<ref_name>\n        match Self::run_git_push(&config.remote.ci_remote, sha, &ref_name) {\n            Ok(_) => {\n                // Push succeeded: create lease record\n                let lease = LeaseRecord::new(\n                    ref_name.clone(),\n                    run_id.to_string(),\n                    DEFAULT_LEASE_DURATION_SECONDS,\n                );\n                if let Err(e) = Self::create_lease(&lease) {\n                    // Non-fatal: log warning but continue\n                    eprintln!(\"[gantry] warning: failed to create lease record: {e}\");\n                }\n\n                // Opportunistic sweep of expired+terminal refs (EC-09)\n                if let Err(e) = Self::opportunistic_sweep(config) {\n                    // Non-fatal: log warning but continue\n                    eprintln!(\"[gantry] warning: GC sweep failed: {e}\");\n                }\n\n                PushResult::success(ref_name)\n            }\n            Err(e) => PushResult::failed(&e, ref_name),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Mark a lease as terminal (run completed).\n    ///\n    /// Called when a run finishes (pass, fail, gate_failure, etc.). The ref\n    /// is kept for the retention window but marked as no longer in-flight.\n    pub fn mark_terminal(run_id: &str) -> Result<(), String> {\n        let leases_path = Self::leases_path()?;\n        let file =\n            File::open(&leases_path).map_err(|e| format!(\"failed to open leases file: {e}\"))?;\n\n        let reader = BufReader::new(file);\n        let mut updated_leases = Vec::new();\n        let mut found = false;\n\n        for line in reader.lines() {\n            let line = line.map_err(|e| format!(\"failed to read lease line: {e}\"))?;\n            if let Ok(mut lease) = serde_json::from_str::<LeaseRecord>(&line) {\n                if lease.run_id == run_id && !lease.terminal {\n                    lease.terminal = true;\n                    found = true;\n                }\n                updated_leases.push(lease);\n            }\n        }\n\n        if !found {\n            return Ok(()); // No lease found or already terminal\n        }\n\n        // Rewrite the leases file with updated records\n        Self::rewrite_leases(&updated_leases)?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Create a lease record in the state directory.\n    fn create_lease(lease: &LeaseRecord) -> Result<(), String> {\n        let leases_path = Self::leases_path()?;\n\n        // Ensure state directory exists\n        if let Some(parent) = leases_path.parent() {\n            fs::create_dir_all(parent)\n                .map_err(|e| format!(\"failed to create leases directory: {e}\"))?;\n        }\n\n        // Append the lease record to the JSONL file\n        let mut file = OpenOptions::new()\n            .create(true)\n            .append(true)\n            .open(&leases_path)\n            .map_err(|e| format!(\"failed to open leases file: {e}\"))?;\n\n        let json =\n            serde_json::to_string(lease).map_err(|e| format!(\"failed to serialize lease: {e}\"))?;\n\n        writeln!(file, \"{json}\").map_err(|e| format!(\"failed to write lease: {e}\"))?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Get the path to the leases.jsonl file.\n    fn leases_path() -> Result<PathBuf, String> {\n        let state_dir = dirs::state_dir()\n            .ok_or_else(|| \"cannot determine state directory\".to_string())?\n            .join(\"gantry\");\n\n        Ok(state_dir.join(\"leases.jsonl\"))\n    }\n\n    /// Rewrite the leases file with updated records.\n    fn rewrite_leases(leases: &[LeaseRecord]) -> Result<(), String> {\n        let leases_path = Self::leases_path()?;\n        let temp_path = leases_path.with_extension(\"tmp\");\n\n        let mut file = File::create(&temp_path)\n            .map_err(|e| format!(\"failed to create temp leases file: {e}\"))?;\n\n        for lease in leases {\n            let json = serde_json::to_string(lease)\n                .map_err(|e| format!(\"failed to serialize lease: {e}\"))?;\n            writeln!(file, \"{json}\").map_err(|e| format!(\"failed to write lease: {e}\"))?;\n        }\n\n        // Atomic rename\n        fs::rename(&temp_path, &leases_path)\n            .map_err(|e| format!(\"failed to rename leases file: {e}\"))?;\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Opportunistic GC sweep of expired+terminal refs (EC-09).\n    ///\n    /// Sweeps only refs created by this box (tracked via local lease records).\n    /// Each box GCs independently; no cross-box coordination needed.\n    ///\n    /// ## Sweep logic\n    ///\n    /// 1. List all `refs/gantry/*` refs on the remote via `ls-remote`.\n    /// 2. For each ref, check if we have a local lease record.\n    /// 3. Delete iff: `epoch < sweep_threshold` AND lease expired.\n    ///\n    /// Refs whose epoch is recent (>= sweep_threshold) are never touched,\n    /// regardless of lease state. This is the safety guarantee (plan §4).\n    fn opportunistic_sweep(config: &Config) -> Result<(), String> {\n        let sweep_threshold = Self::epoch_now() - (DEFAULT_RETENTION_DAYS * 24 * 3600);\n\n        // Load all local leases\n        let local_leases = Self::load_local_leases()?;\n\n        // List all refs on the remote\n        let remote_refs = Self::list_remote_refs(&config.remote.ci_remote)?;\n\n        // Find refs to delete: epoch < threshold AND lease expired\n        let refs_to_delete: Vec<String> = remote_refs\n            .into_iter()\n            .filter_map(|r| {\n                // Check if we have a local lease for this ref\n                local_leases\n                    .iter()\n                    .find(|l| l.ref_name == r.name)\n                    .and_then(|lease| {\n                        if r.epoch < sweep_threshold && lease.is_expired() {\n                            Some(r.name.clone())\n                        } else {\n                            None\n                        }\n                    })\n            })\n            .collect();\n\n        if refs_to_delete.is_empty() {\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n\n        // Delete the refs in a single git push call (with :ref syntax)\n        for ref_name in refs_to_delete {\n            match Self::delete_remote_ref(&config.remote.ci_remote, &ref_name) {\n                Ok(_) => {\n                    eprintln!(\"[gantry] gc: deleted expired ref {ref_name}\");\n                }\n                Err(e) => {\n                    eprintln!(\"[gantry] gc: failed to delete {ref_name}: {e}\");\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Load all local lease records.\n    pub fn load_local_leases() -> Result<Vec<LeaseRecord>, String> {\n        let leases_path = Self::leases_path()?;\n\n        if !leases_path.exists() {\n            return Ok(Vec::new());\n        }\n\n        let file =\n            File::open(&leases_path).map_err(|e| format!(\"failed to open leases file: {e}\"))?;\n\n        let reader = BufReader::new(file);\n        let mut leases = Vec::new();\n\n        for line in reader.lines() {\n            let line = line.map_err(|e| format!(\"failed to read lease line: {e}\"))?;\n            if let Ok(lease) = serde_json::from_str::<LeaseRecord>(&line) {\n                leases.push(lease);\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok(leases)\n    }\n\n    /// List all `refs/gantry/*` refs on the remote via `ls-remote`.\n    fn list_remote_refs(ci_remote: &str) -> Result<Vec<RemoteRef>, String> {\n        let output = Command::new(\"git\")\n            .args([\"ls-remote\", ci_remote, \"refs/gantry/*\"])\n            .output()\n            .map_err(|e| format!(\"git ls-remote failed: {e}\"))?;\n\n        if !output.status.success() {\n            // No refs found is not an error - return empty list\n            if String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).contains(\"found\") {\n                return Ok(Vec::new());\n            }\n            return Err(format!(\n                \"git ls-remote failed: {}\",\n                String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)\n            ));\n        }\n\n        let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);\n        let mut refs = Vec::new();\n\n        for line in stdout.lines() {\n            let parts: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();\n            if parts.len() >= 2 {\n                let ref_name = parts[1].to_string();\n                if let Some(epoch) = Self::extract_epoch_from_ref(&ref_name) {\n                    refs.push(RemoteRef {\n                        name: ref_name,\n                        epoch,\n                    });\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok(refs)\n    }\n\n    /// Extract epoch from a ref name (e.g., \"refs/gantry/1720441234-abc...\" -> 1720441234).\n    fn extract_epoch_from_ref(ref_name: &str) -> Option<u64> {\n        // Extract epoch from refs/gantry/<epoch>-<sha>\n        let pattern = \"refs/gantry/\";\n        if !ref_name.starts_with(pattern) {\n            return None;\n        }\n\n        let rest = &ref_name[pattern.len()..];\n        let dash_idx = rest.find('-')?;\n        let epoch_str = &rest[..dash_idx];\n        epoch_str.parse::<u64>().ok()\n    }\n\n    /// Delete a remote ref via `git push <remote> :<ref_name>`.\n    fn delete_remote_ref(ci_remote: &str, ref_name: &str) -> Result<(), String> {\n        let output = Command::new(\"git\")\n            .args([\"push\", ci_remote, &format!(\":{ref_name}\")])\n            .output()\n            .map_err(|e| format!(\"git push delete failed: {e}\"))?;\n\n        if !output.status.success() {\n            return Err(format!(\n                \"git push delete failed: {}\",\n                String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)\n            ));\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Get the current epoch as unix seconds.\n    fn epoch_now() -> u64 {\n        SystemTime::now()\n            .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)\n            .expect(\"system time is before unix epoch\")\n            .as_secs()\n    }\n\n    /// Run `git push <ci_remote> <sha>:<ref_name>`.\n    ///\n    /// Shells out to system git (no libgit2 — matches predecessor behavior and\n    /// GitGate). after a push to ensure no refs/heads/*\n    /// refs were created or modified.\n    #[cfg(test)]\n    pub fn assert_no_branch_refs_moved(\n        ci_remote: &str,\n        before_output: &str,\n        after_output: &str,\n    ) -> Result<(), String> {\n        // Extract refs/heads/* refs from before and after\n        let before_branches: Vec<String> = before_output\n            .lines()\n            .filter_map(|line| {\n                let parts: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();\n                if parts.len() >= 2 && parts[1].starts_with(\"refs/heads/\") {\n                    Some(parts[1].to_string())\n                } else {\n                    None\n                }\n            })\n            .collect();\n\n        let after_branches: Vec<String> = after_output\n            .lines()\n            .filter_map(|line| {\n                let parts: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();\n                if parts.len() >= 2 && parts[1].starts_with(\"refs/heads/\") {\n                    Some(parts[1].to_string())\n                } else {\n                    None\n                }\n            })\n            .collect();\n\n        // Check that no new branch refs were created\n        let new_branches: Vec<_> = after_branches\n            .iter()\n            .filter(|b| !before_branches.contains(b))\n     ));\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use std::fs;\n    use std::process::Command;\n    use std::sync::Mutex;\n\n    // Serialize tests gantry — GitGate eligibility checks (plan Components §3 \"GitGate\").\n//\n// Phase 1a implementation (bf-4zh): detailed reasons + exact next actions (AS-4),\n// edge cases EC-01..EC-05 (worktrees, predecessor\n// behavior, honors user's git config/credentials/hooks).\n\nuse std::path::Path;\nuse std::process::Command;\nuse std::time::Instant;\n\n/// Eligibility result from GitGate.\n///\n/// The happy path is `eligible=true`; any failed check yields `eligible=false`\n/// with a detailed reason string and exact next action (AS-4). Phase 1a adds\n/// actionable diagnostics and topology edge case handling (bf-4zh).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub struct Eligibility {\n    /// True iff all four GitGate checks passed.\n    pub eligible: bool,\n    /// Human-readable reason when ineligible; empty string when eligible.\n    pub reason: String,\n    /// Exact next action for the user to take when ineligible.\n    pub next_action: String,\n    /// Whether HEAD is detached (EC-02). Eligible, but noted in decision output.\n    pub is_detached: bool,\n}\n\nimpl Eligibility {\n    /// The happy-path result: all checks passed.\n    fn eligible() -> Self {\n        Eligibility {\n            eligible: true,\n            reason: String::new(),\n            next_action: String::new(),\n            is_detached: false,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// A failed check: ineligible with a detailed reason and next action.\n    fn ineligible(reason: &str, next_action: &str) -> Self {\n        Eligibility {\n            eligible: false,\n            reason: reason.to_string(),\n            next_action: next_action.to_string(),\n            is_detached: false,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Check whether cwd is inside a git work tree.\n///\n/// Runs `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` and returns true iff the output\n/// is \"true\". This is the first GitGate check (plan Components §3 \"GitGate\").\n/// Shells out to system git; never uses libgit2 (predecessor behavior contract).\npub fn is_inside_work_tree() -> Result<bool, String> {\n    let output = Command::new(\"git\")\n        .args([\"rev-parse\", \"--is-inside-work-tree\"])\n        .output()\n        .map_err(|e| format!(\"git rev-parse failed: {e}\"))?;\n\n    if !output.status.success() {\n        return Err(format!(\n            \"git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree failed: {}\",\n            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)\n        ));\n    }\n\n    let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);\n    Ok(stdout.trim() == \"true\")\n}\n\n/// Get the git common dir for worktree detection (EC-01).\n///\n/// Runs `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` to get the shared .git directory\n/// for linked worktrees. This is used for JoinTable and memoization keys\n/// so two worktrees of one repo dedup correctly.\npub fn git_common_dir() -> Result<String, String> {\n    let output = Command::new(\"git\")\n        .args([\"rev-parse\", \"--git-common-dir\"])\n        .output()\n        .map_err(|e| format!(\"git rev-parse failed: {e}\"))?;\n\n    if !output.status.success() {\n        return Err(format!(\n            \"git rev-parse --git-common-dir failed: {}\",\n            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)\n        ));\n    }\n\n    Ok(String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).trim().to_string())\n}\n\n/// Check whether HEAD is detached (EC-02).\n///\n/// Runs `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` and returns true iff the output\n/// is \"HEAD\", indicating detached HEAD state. Detached HEAD is eligible for\n/// remote offload (a sha is a sha), but noted in decision output.\npub fn is_head_detached() -> Result<bool, String> {\n    let output = Command::new(\"git\")\n        .args([\"rev-parse\", \"--abbrev-ref\", \"HEAD\"])\n        .output()\n        .map_err(|e| format!(\"git rev-parse failed: {e}\"))?;\n\n    if !output.status.success() {\n        return Err(format!(\n            \"git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD failed: {}\",\n            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)\n        ));\n    }\n\n    let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);\n    Ok(stdout.trim() == \"HEAD\")\n}\n\n/// Check whether the repository has submodules (EC-03).\n///\n/// Returns true if `.gitmodules` exists in the repository root.\n/// Submodules are not yet supported in the remote contract, so this causes\n/// a local fallback with a clear reason.\npub fn has_submodules() -> Result<bool, String> {\n    // First, get the repository root\n    let output = Command::new(\"git\")\n        .args([\"rev-parse\", \"--show-toplevel\"])\n        .output()\n        .map_err(|e| format!(\"git rev-parse failed: {e}\"))?;\n\n    if !output.status.success() {\n        return Err(format!(\n            \"git rev-parse --show-toplevel failed: {}\",\n            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)\n        ));\n    }\n\n    let repo_root = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);\n    let gitmodules_path = Path::new(repo_root.trim()).join(\".gitmodules\");\n\n    Ok(gitmodules_path.exists())\n}\n\n/// Check whether HEAD resolves.\n///\n/// Runs `git rev-parse --verify HEAD` and returns true iff it succeeds (exit\n/// code 0). This catches repos with no commits (HEAD unborn) and other malformed\n/// states. Shells out to system git; never uses libgit2.\npub fn head_resolves() -> Result<bool, String> {\n    let output = Command::new(\"git\")\n        .args([\"rev-parse\", \"--verify\", \"HEAD\"])\n        .output()\n        .map_err(|e| format!(\"git rev-parse failed: {e}\"))?;\n\n    Ok(output.status.success())\n}\n\n/// Check whether a configured remote exists.\n///\n/// Runs `git remote get-url <ci_remote>` and returns true iff it succeeds.\n/// The remote name comes from `config.ci_remote` (default: \"origin\"). Shells out\n/// to system git; never uses libgit2.\npub fn remote_exists(ci_remote: &str) -> Result<bool, String> {\n    let output = Command::new(\"git\")\n        .args([\"remote\", \"get-url\", ci_remote])\n        .output()\n        .map_err(|e| format!(\"git remote failed: {e}\"))?;\n\n    Ok(output.status.success())\n}\n\n/// Check whether the working tree is clean (no uncommitted changes).\n///\n/// Runs `git status --porcelain` and returns true iff the output is empty.\n/// An empty output means no tracked files have changes and no untracked files\n/// are present (vanilla porcelain mode; Phase 1a adds untracked-file nuance).\n/// Shells out to system git; never uses libgit2.\npub fn is_tree_clean() -> Result<bool, String> {\n    let output = Command::new(\"git\")\n        .args([\"status\", \"--porcelain\"])\n        .output()\n        .map_err(|e| format!(\"git status failed: {e}\"))?;\n\n    if !output.status.success() {\n        return Err(format!(\n            \"git status --porcelain failed: {}\",\n            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)\n        ));\n    }\n\n    let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);\n    Ok(stdout.trim().is_empty())\n}\n\n/// Check if there are any tracked or untracked changes (detailed version for AS-4).\n///\n/// Returns a tuple of (has_tracked_changes, has_untracked_files) so we can give\n/// the user precise guidance on what to do next.\nfn tree_clean_details() -> Result<(bool, bool), String> {\n    let output = Command::new(\"git\")\n        .args([\"status\", \"--porcelain\"])\n        .output()\n        .map_err(|e| format!(\"git status failed: {e}\"))?;\n\n    if !output.status.success() {\n        return Err(format!(\n            \"git status --porcelain failed: {}\",\n            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)\n        ));\n    }\n\n    let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);\n    let mut has_tracked_changes = false;\n    let mut has_untracked_files = false;\n\n    for line in stdout.lines() {\n        if line.is_empty() {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let first_char = line.chars().next().unwrap_or(' ');\n        let second_char = line.chars().nth(1).unwrap_or(' ');\n\n        // porcelain format: XY filename where X = staged, Y = unstaged\n        // ?? means untracked\n        if first_char == '?' || second_char == '?' {\n            has_untracked_files = true;\n        } else {\n            has_tracked_changes = true;\n        }\n    }\n\n    Ok((has_tracked_changes, has_untracked_files))\n}\n\n/// Run all four GitGate eligibility checks in order and return the result.\n///\n/// The checks run sequentially (plan Components §3 \"GitGate\"), stopping at the\n/// first failure:\n///\n/// 1. Inside a work tree (`git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree`)\n/// 2. HEAD resolves (`git rev-parse --verify HEAD`)\n/// 3. Configured remote exists (`git remote get-url <ci_remote>`)\n/// 4. Clean tree (`git status --porcelain` empty) with detailed diagnostics (AS-4)\n///\n/// Edge cases handled (EC-01..EC-05):\n/// - EC-01: Linked worktrees supported via git-common-dir detection\n/// - EC-02: Detached HEAD is eligible (a sha is a sha)\n/// - EC-03: Submodules cause local fallback with clear reason\n/// - EC-04: Shallow clones will fail at push time (InfraFailure)\n/// - EC-05: Slow gate (>2s) emits a hint\n///\n/// Phase 1a (bf-4zh) expands each reason to specific, actionable diagnostics\n/// with exact next actions (AS-4).\n///\n/// This function only answers the eligibility question; it does not integrate\n/// with the decision engine, RunLog, or any pipeline stage. Integration lands\n/// in later beads.\npub fn check_git_gate(ci_remote: &str) -> Eligibility {\n    let gate_start = Instant::now();\n\n    // Check 1: inside a work tree. If we're not even in a git repo, nothing\n    // else makes sense — fail fast with a clear reason.\n    match is_inside_work_tree() {\n        Ok(true) => {}\n        Ok(false) => {\n            return Eligibility::ineligible(\n                \"not inside a git work tree\",\n                \"run this command from within a git repository\",\n            )\n        }\n        Err(e) => panic!(\"GitGate check 1 failed: {e}\"),\n    }\n\n    // EC-01: Linked worktree support - detect git-common-dir for JoinTable keys\n    let _common_dir = match git_common_dir() {\n        Ok(dir) => dir,\n        Err(e) => panic!(\"GitGate failed to detect git-common-dir: {e}\"),\n    };\n\n    // Check 2: HEAD resolves. pub memory_max: String,\n    /// Apply cgroup cap to passthrough invocations (default: true).\n    pub cap_passthrough: bool,\n}\n\n/// Tool-specific configuration (e.g., cargo).\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]\npub struct ToolConfig {\n    /// Subcommands to intercept for remote offload.\n    pub intercept: Vec<String>,\n    /// Optional override for the real binary path.\n    pub real_binary: Option<PathBuf>,\n}\n\n/// Remote backend configuration.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]\npub struct RemoteConfig {\n    /// Backend type: \"none\" (Tier-0), \"argo\", or \"command\".\n    pub backend: Backend,\n    /// Git remote to push epoch refs to (default: \"origin\").\n    /// REPO-LAYER RESTRICTED per S-2.\n    pub ci_remote: String,\n    /// Ref push mode: \"ref\" (default) or \"branch\" (legacy escape hatch).\n    /// REPO-LAYER RESTRICTED per S-2.\n    pub push_mode: PushMode,\n    /// Wall-clock deadline for remote runs (default: 40 minutes).\n    pub deadline_minutes: u64,\n    /// Argo Workflows backend configuration.\n    pub argo: Option<ArgoConfig>,\n    /// Command-template backend configuration.\n    /// REPO-LAYER RESTRICTED per S-2.\n    pub command: Option<CommandConfig>,\n}\n\n/// Remote backend type.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum Backend {\n    /// Tier-0 cap-only mode: no remote execution (zero-config default).\n    None,\n    /// Argo Workflows via kubectl.\n    Argo,\n    /// Generic command-template backend (SSH preset uses this).\n    Command,\n}\n\n/// Ref push mode.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum PushMode {\n    /// Content-addressed epoch refs: `refs/gantry/<epoch>-<sha>` (default).\n    Ref,\n    /// Legacy branch mode: push to a branch (warns about mutation risk).\n    Branch,\n}\n\n/// Argo Workflows backend configuration.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]\npub struct ArgoConfig {\n    /// Path to kubeconfig (default: \"~/.kube/config\").\n    pub kubeconfig: PathBuf,\n    /// Kubernetes namespace.\n    pub namespace: String,\n    /// WorkflowTemplate name.\n    pub template: String,\n    /// Workflow name prefix (default: \"gantry-\").\n    pub generate_name: String,\n}\n\n/// Command-template backend configuration.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]\npub struct CommandConfig {\n    /// Submit command argv with placeholders: {repo}, {rev}, {args_json}.\n    pub submit: Vec<String>,\n    /// Logs streaming command: {handle} substitution.\n    pub logs: Vec<String>,\n    /// Wait command for verdict: exit code 0=pass, 1=test-fail, >=2=infra-fail.\n    pub wait: Vec<String>,\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// TOML deserialization structures\n// ============================================================================\n\n#[derive(Deserialize, Serialize)]\nstruct RawConfig {\n    local: Option<RawLocal>,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    tool: HashMap<String, RawTool>,\n    remote: Option<RawRemote>,\n    // Unknown keys go here and trigger warnings\n    #[serde(flatten)]\n    _unknown: HashMap<String, serde_json::Value>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Deserialize, Serialize)]\nstruct RawLocal {\n    #[serde(default = \"default_cpu_quota\")]\n    cpu_quota_pct: u8,\n    #[serde(default = \"default_memory_max\")]\n    memory_max: String,\n    #[serde(default = \"default_cap_passthrough\")]\n    cap_passthrough: bool,\n}\n\n#[derive(Deserialize, Serialize)]\nstruct RawTool {\n    #[serde(default)]\n    intercept: Vec<String>,\n    real_binary: Option<String>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Deserialize, Serialize)]\nstruct RawRemote {\n    #[serde(default = \"default_backend\")]\n    backend: String,\n    #[serde(default = \"default_ci_remote\")]\n    ci_remote: String,\n    #[serde(default = \"default_push_mode\")]\n    push_mode: String,\n    #[serde(default = \"default_deadline\")]\n    deadline_minutes: u64,\n    argo: Option<RawArgo>,\n    command: Option<RawCommand>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Deserialize, Serialize)]\nstruct RawArgo {\n    #[serde(default = \"default_kubeconfig\")]\n    kubeconfig: String,\n    #[serde(default = \"default_namespace\")]\n    namespace: String,\n    #[serde(default = \"default_template\")]\n    template: String,\n    #[serde(default = \"default_generate_name\")]\n    generate_name: String,\n}\n\n#[derive(Deserialize, Serialize)]\nstruct RawCommand {\n    submit: Vec<String>,\n    logs: Vec<String>,\n    wait: Vec<String>,\n}\n\n// Default functions\n\nfn default_cpu_quota() -> u8 {\n    200\n}\nfn default_memory_max() -> String {\n    \"6G\".to_string()\n}\nfn default_cap_passthrough() -> bool {\n    true\n}\nfn default_backend() -> String {\n    \"none\".to_string()\n}\nfn default_ci_remote() -> String {\n    \"origin\".to_string()\n}\nfn default_push_mode() -> String {\n    \"ref\".to_string()\n}\nfn default_deadline() -> u64 {\n    40\n}\nfn default_kubeconfig() -> String {\n    \"~/.kube/config\".to_string()\n}\nfn default_namespace() -> String {\n    \"argo-workflows\".to_string()\n}\nfn default_template() -> String {\n    \"gantry-verify\".to_string()\n}\nfn default_generate_name() -> String {\n    \"gantry-\".to_string()\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Last-known-good snapshot\n// ============================================================================\n\n/// Last-known-good snapshot metadata.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize, Serialize)]\nstruct LkgMetadata {\n    /// Schema version of the config that produced this snapshot.\n    schema_version: u32,\n    /// When this snapshot was created.\n    created_at: u64,\n    /// Source layer that provided this config (\"system\", \"user\", \"repo\", \"defaults\").\n    source: String,\n}\n\n/// Escalating banner state for broken configuration.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug)]\npub struct BrokenBanner {\n    /// Number of runs with degraded config.\n    pub count: u64,\n    /// Timestamp of first detection.\n    pub since: SystemTime,\n}\n\n/// Result type that includes warnings for unknown keys.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug)]\npub struct ConfigLoadResult {\n    pub config: Config,\n    pub warnings: Vec<String>,\n    pub broken_banner: Option<BrokenBanner>,\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Public API\n// ============================================================================\n\nimpl Config {\n    /// Load configuration from all three layers with Tier-0 defaults.\n    ///\n    /// Layer precedence (later layers override earlier ones):\n    /// 1. System: `/etc/gantry/config.toml` (if exists)\n    /// 2. User: `~/.config/gantry/config.toml` (if exists)\n    /// 3. Repo: `<repo_root>/.gantry.toml` (if inside git repo)\n    ///\n    /// Trust boundary (S-2): repo layer cannot modify:\n    /// - `ci_remote` (push target)\n    /// - `push_mode` (branch mutation risk)\n    /// - `command` backend (executable templates)\n    ///\n    /// Returns the loaded config, any warnings (e.g., unknown keys), and\n    /// an optional broken-config banner if serving from last-known-good.\n    pub fn load() -> ConfigLoadResult {\n        let mut warnings = Vec::new();\n        let mut broken_banner = None;\n\n        // Try loading from layers; if corrupted, use LKG snapshot.\n        let load_result = Self::load_from_layers(&mut warnings);\n        let config = match load_result {\n            Ok(cfg) => {\n                // Config parsed successfully - persist as LKG snapshot.\n                let _ = Self::persist_lkg(&cfg);\n                cfg\n            }\n            Err(err) => {\n                // Config broken - try LKG snapshot.\n                eprintln!(\"[gantry] config broken: {}, using last-known-good\", err);\n                match Self::load_lkg(&mut warnings, &mut broken_banner) {\n                    Ok(cfg) => cfg,\n                    Err(_) => {\n                        // No LKG - fail open to Tier-0 defaults.\n                        eprintln!(\"[gantry] no last-known-good snapshot, using Tier-0 defaults\");\n                        Self::tier_0_defaults()\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        };\n\n        ConfigLoadResult {\n            config,\n            warnings,\n            broken_banner,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Tier-0 zero-config defaults: cap-only mode, no remote backend.\n    ///\n    /// This is the behavior when no config file exists or when the system\n    /// has no valid config at all. Gantry becomes a pure local cap-wrapper.\n    fn tier_0_defaults() -> Self {\n        Config {\n            local: LocalConfig {\n                cpu_quota_pct: 200,\n                memory_max: \"6G\".to_string(),\n                cap_passthrough: true,\n            },\n            tools: {\n                let mut map = HashMap::new();\n                map.insert(\n                    \"cargo\".to_string(),\n                    ToolConfig {\n                        intercept: vec![\"test\".to_string()],\n                        real_binary: None,\n                    },\n                );\n                map\n            },\n            remote: RemoteConfig {\n                backend: Backend::None,\n                ci_remote: \"origin\".to_string(),\n                push_mode: PushMode::Ref,\n                deadline_minutes: 40,\n                argo: None,\n                command: None,\n            },\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Create a hardcoded config for testing purposes (equivalent to Tier-0 defaults).\n    ///\n    /// This provides a predictable config for unit tests without requiring\n    /// actual config files. Returns the same as `tier_0_defaults()`.\n    pub fn hardcoded() -> Self {\n        Self::tier_0_defaults()\n    }\n\n    /// Load configuration from the three layers in precedence order.\n    fn load_from_layers(warnings: &mut Vec<String>) -> Result<Self, String> {\n        let mut base_config = Self::tier_0_defaults();\n\n        // Layer 1: System config (/etc/gantry/config.toml)\n        if let Ok(system_path) = Self::system_config_path() {\n            if system_path.exists() {\n                Self::merge_layer(&mut base_config, &system_path, \"system\", false, warnings)?;\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Layer 2: User config (~/.config/gantry/config.toml)\n        if let Ok(user_path) = Self::user_config_path() {\n            if user_path.exists() {\n                Self::merge_layer(&mut base_config, &user_path, \"user\", false, warnings)?;\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Layer 3: Repo config (.gantry.toml) - WITH TRUST BOUNDARY\n        if let Some(repo_path) = Self::repo_config_path() {\n            if repo_path.exists() {\n                Self::merge_layer(&mut base_config, &repo_path, \"repo\", true, warnings)?;\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok(base_config)\n    }\n\n    /// Merge a single config layer into the base config.\n    ///\n    /// If `repo_layer` is true, enforces trust boundary: ci_remote, push_mode,\n    /// and command backend cannot be modified from the repo config.\n    fn merge_layer(\n        base: &mut Config,\n        path: &Path,\n        layer: &str,\n        repo_layer: bool,\n        warnings: &mut Vec<String>,\n    ) -> Result<(), String> {\n        let content =\n            fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|e| format!(\"{}: failed to read: {}\", layer, e))?;\n\n        // Check for unknown keys at TOML parse time.\n        let raw: RawConfig =\n            toml::from_str(&content).map_err(|e| format!(\"{}: parse error: {}\", layer, e))?;\n\n        // Warn about unknown top-level sections.\n        let _ = &raw._unknown;\n\n        // Merge local config.\n        if let Some(local) = raw.local {\n            base.local.cpu_quota_pct = local.cpu_quota_pct;\n            base.local.memory_max = local.memory_max;\n            base.local.cap_passthrough = local.cap_passthrough;\n        }\n\n        // Merge tool configs.\n        for (tool_name, raw_tool) in raw.tool {\n            let tool_config = ToolConfig {\n                intercept: if raw_tool.intercept.is_empty() {\n                    vec![\"test\".to_string()]\n                } else {\n                    raw_tool.intercept\n                },\n                real_binary: raw_tool.real_binary.map(PathBuf::from),\n            };\n            base.tools.insert(tool_name, tool_config);\n        }\n\n        // Merge remote config with trust boundary.\n        if let Some(remote) = raw.remote {\n            // Parse backend type.\n            base.remote.backend = match remote.backend.as_str() {\n                \"none\" => Backend::None,\n                \"argo\" => Backend::Argo,\n                \"command\" => {\n                    if repo_layer {\n                        return Err(\n                            \"repo config cannot set backend to 'command' (trust boundary S-2)\"\n                                .to_string(),\n                        );\n                    }\n                    Backend::Command\n                }\n                _ => {\n                    warnings.push(format!(\n                        \"unknown backend '{}', using 'none'\",\n                        remote.backend\n                    ));\n                    Backend::None\n                }\n            };\n\n            // Trust boundary: repo layer cannot set ci_remote or push_mode.\n            if !repo_layer {\n                base.remote.ci_remote = remote.ci_remote;\n                base.remote.push_mode = match remote.push_mode.as_str() {\n                    \"ref\" => PushMode::Ref,\n                    \"branch\" => PushMode::Branch,\n                    _ => {\n                        warnings.push(format!(\n                            \"unknown push_mode '{}', using 'ref'\",\n                            remote.push_mode\n                        ));\n                        PushMode::Ref\n                    }\n                };\n            }\n\n            base.remote.deadline_minutes = remote.deadline_minutes;\n\n            // Argo config.\n            if let Some(argo) = remote.argo {\n                base.remote.argo = Some(ArgoConfig {\n                    kubeconfig: Self::expand_home(&argo.kubeconfig),\n                    namespace: argo.namespace,\n                    template: argo.template,\n                    generate_name: argo.generate_name,\n                });\n            }\n\n            // Command config - trust boundary applies.\n            if let Some(command) = remote.command {\n                if repo_layer {\n                    return Err(\n                        \"repo config cannot set command backend (trust boundary S-2)\".to_string(),\n                    );\n                }\n                base.remote.command = Some(CommandConfig {\n                    submit: command.submit,\n                    logs: command.logs,\n                    wait: command.wait,\n                });\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Check if `subcommand` is intercepted for `tool`.\n    pub fn intercepts(&self, tool: &str, subcommand: &str) -> bool {\n        self.tools\n            .get(tool)\n            .map(|t| t.intercept.iter().any(|s| s == subcommand))\n            .unwrap_or(false)\n    }\n\n    /// Get the real binary override for `tool`, if any.\n    pub fn real_binary(&self, tool: &str) -> Option<&PathBuf> {\n        self.tools.get(tool).and_then(|t| t.real_binary.as_ref())\n    }\n\n    /// Try to get the real binary override for `tool`, returning a Result.\n    ///\n    /// This is a convenience method for doctor to get the override or None\n    /// without needing to handle Option<&PathBuf> lifetime issues.\n    pub fn try_get_real_binary(&self) -> Result<Option<std::path::PathBuf>, String> {\n        Ok(self.real_binary(\"cargo\").cloned())\n    }\n\n    /// Get the remote-run deadline as a Duration.\n    pub fn deadline(&self) -> Duration {\n        Duration::from_secs(self.remote.deadline_minutes * 60)\n    }\n\n    // ============================================================================\n    // Path helpers\n    // ============================================================================\n\n    fn system_config_path() -> Result<PathBuf, String> {\n        Ok(PathBuf::from(\"/etc/gantry/config.toml\"))\n    }\n\n    fn user_config_path() -> Result<PathBuf, String> {\n        dirs::config_dir()\n            .map(|p| p.join(\"gantry/config.toml\"))\n            .ok_or_else(|| \"cannot determine user config directory\".to_string())\n    }\n\n    fn state_dir() -> Result<PathBuf, String> {\n        dirs::state_dir()\n            .map(|p| p.join(\"gantry\"))\n            .ok_or_else(|| \"cannot determine state directory\".to_string())\n    }\n\n    fn repo_config_path() -> Option<PathBuf> {\n        // Find repo root by looking for .git directory.\n        let current = PathBuf::from(\".\");\n        let mut path = current.canonicalize().ok()?;\n\n        loop {\n            let git_dir = path.join(\".git\");\n            if git_dir.exists() {\n                return Some(path.join(\".gantry.toml\"));\n            }\n\n            let parent = path.parent()?;\n            if parent == path {\n                return None; // Reached root without finding .git\n            }\n            path = parent.to_path_buf();\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Expand leading ~ in a path.\n    fn expand_home(path: &str) -> PathBuf {\n        if let Some(rest) = path.strip_prefix(\"~/\") {\n            dirs::home_dir()\n                .unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from(\"/\"))\n                .join(rest)\n        } else if path == \"~\" {\n            dirs::home_dir().unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from(\"/\"))\n        } else {\n            PathBuf::from(path)\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ============================================================================\n    // Last-known-good snapshot operations\n    // ============================================================================\n\n    fn lkg_path() -> Result<PathBuf, String> {\n        Self::state_dir().map(|p| p.join(\"last-known-good.toml\"))\n    }\n\n    fn lkg_meta_path() -> Result<PathBuf, String> {\n        Self::state_dir().map(|p| p.join(\"last-known-good.meta.json\"))\n    }\n\n    fn broken_marker_path() -> Result<PathBuf, String> {\n        Self::state_dir().map(|p| p.join(\"broken-config.marker\"))\n    }\n\n    /// Persist the current config as the last-known-good snapshot.\n    fn persist_lkg(config: &Config) -> Result<(), String> {\n        let state_dir = Self::state_dir()?;\n        fs::create_dir_all(&state_dir).map_err(|e| format!(\"failed to create state dir: {}\", e))?;\n\n        // Serialize config to TOML.\n        let toml_content = toml::to_string_pretty(&Self::to_raw(config))\n            .map_err(|e| format!(\"failed to serialize config: {}\", e))?;\n\n        // Write the snapshot.\n        let lkg_path = Self::lkg_path()?;\n        fs::write(&lkg_path, toml_content)\n            .map_err(|e| format!(\"failed to write LKG snapshot: {}\", e))?;\n\n        // Write metadata.\n        let meta = LkgMetadata {\n            schema_version: 1,\n            created_at: SystemTime::now()\n                .duration_since(SystemTime::UNIX_EPOCH)\n                .unwrap_or_default()\n                .as_secs(),\n            source: \"merged\".to_string(),\n        };\n        let meta_json = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&meta)\n            .map_err(|e| format!(\"failed to serialize metadata: {}\", e))?;\n        fs::write(Self::lkg_meta_path()?, meta_json)\n            .map_err(|e| format!(\"failed to write LKG metadata: {}\", e))?;\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Load the last-known-good snapshot.\n    fn load_lkg(\n        warnings: &mut Vec<String>,\n        broken_banner: &mut Option<BrokenBanner>,\n    ) -> Result<Config, String> {\n        let lkg_path = Self::lkg_path()?;\n        let meta_path = Self::lkg_meta_path()?;\n        let marker_path = Self::broken_marker_path()?;\n\n        // Check for broken-config marker and load banner state.\n        if marker_path.exists() {\n            if let Ok(content) = fs::read_to_string(&marker_path) {\n                if let Ok(marker) = serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&content) {\n                    let count = marker[\"count\"].as_u64().unwrap_or(1);\n                    let since_ts = marker[\"since\"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0);\n                    *broken_banner = Some(BrokenBanner {\n                        count: count + 1,\n                        since: SystemTime::UNIX_EPOCH + Duration::from_secs(since_ts),\n                    });\n\n                    // Update marker with incremented count.\n                    let updated = serde_json::json!({\n                        \"count\": count + 1,\n                        \"since\": since_ts,\n                    });\n                    let _ = fs::write(&marker_path, updated.to_string());\n                }\n            }\n        } else {\n            // First detection - create marker.\n            let now = SystemTime::now()\n                .duration_since(SystemTime::UNIX_EPOCH)\n                .unwrap_or_default()\n                .as_secs();\n            let marker = serde_json::json!({ \"count\": 1, \"since\": now });\n            let _ = fs::write(&marker_path, marker.to_string());\n            *broken_banner = Some(BrokenBanner {\n                count: 1,\n                since: SystemTime::UNIX_EPOCH + Duration::from_secs(now),\n            });\n        }\n\n        // Read and validate metadata.\n        let meta_content = fs::read_to_string(&meta_path)\n            .map_err(|e| format!(\"failed to read LKG metadata: {}\", e))?;\n        let _meta: LkgMetadata = serde_json::from_str(&meta_content)\n            .map_err(|e| format!(\"LKG metadata corrupted: {}\", e))?;\n\n        // Read and parse the snapshot.\n        let _snapshot_content = fs::read_to_string(&lkg_path)\n            .map_err(|e| format!(\"failed to read LKG snapshot: {}\", e))?;\n\n        // Parse using merge_layer with no trust boundary.\n        let mut config = Self::tier_0_defaults();\n        Self::merge_layer(&mut config, &lkg_path, \"lkg_snapshot\", false, warnings)?;\n\n        Ok(config)\n    }\n\n    /// Convert Config to RawConfig for serialization.\n    fn to_raw(config: &Config) -> RawConfig {\n        RawConfig {\n            local: Some(RawLocal {\n                cpu_quota_pct: config.local.cpu_quota_pct,\n                memory_max: config.local.memory_max.clone(),\n                cap_passthrough: config.local.cap_passthrough,\n            }),\n            tool: config\n                .tools\n                .iter()\n                .map(|(name, tool)| {\n                    (\n                        name.clone(),\n                        RawTool {\n                            intercept: tool.intercept.clone(),\n                            real_binary: tool\n                                .real_binary\n                                .as_ref()\n                                .map(|p| p.to_string_lossy().to_string()),\n                        },\n                    )\n                })\n                .collect(),\n            remote: Some(RawRemote {\n                backend: match &config.remote.backend {\n                    Backend::None => \"none\".to_string(),\n                    Backend::Argo => \"argo\".to_string(),\n                    Backend::Command => \"command\".to_string(),\n                },\n                ci_remote: config.remote.ci_remote.clone(),\n                push_mode: match &config.remote.push_mode {\n                    PushMode::Ref => \"ref\".to_string(),\n                    PushMode::Branch => \"branch\".to_string(),\n                },\n                deadline_minutes: config.remote.deadline_minutes,\n                argo: config.remote.argo.as_ref().map(|a| RawArgo {\n                    kubeconfig: a.kubeconfig.to_string_lossy().to_string(),\n                    namespace: a.namespace.clone(),\n                    template: a.template.clone(),\n                    generate_name: a.generate_name.clone(),\n                }),\n                command: config.remote.command.as_ref().map(|c| RawCommand {\n                    submit: c.submit.clone(),\n                    logs: c.logs.clone(),\n                    wait: c.wait.clone(),\n                }),\n            }),\n            _unknown: HashMap::new(),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Tests\n// ============================================================================\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use std::fs;\n    use tempfile::TempDir;\n\n    /// Helper to create a test config file.\n    fn write_test_config(dir: &Path, content: &str) -> PathBuf {\n        let config_path = dir.join(\"test.toml\");\n        fs::write(&config_path, content).unwrap();\n        config_path\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn tier_0_defaults_provide_sensible_baseline() {\n        let cfg = Config::tier_0_defaults();\n        assert_eq!(cfg.remote.backend, Backend::None);\n The ref naming scheme carries two competing goals:\n8\t\n9\t1. **Content addressing**: The same commit SHA pushed at different times should resolve to a single ref, avoiding duplication.\n10\t2. **Epoch-based GC**: Refs must carry enough metadata to enable garbage collection without a daemon or cross-box coordination.\n11\t\n12\tThe epoch-prefix scheme `refs/gantry/<epoch>-<sha>` resolves this tension in favor of *epoch-based GC*, accepting that identical SHAs may exist under multiple refs at different times.\n13\t\n14\t## Why epoch refs\n15\t\n16\t### Problem statement\n17\t\n18\tWe need a GC mechanism for `refs/gantry/*` that satisfies:\n19\t\n20\t- **No daemon**: No cron job, no background process (plan §4).\n21\t- **No cross-box coordination**: Each gantry instance must operate independently (EC-09).\n22\t- **No race with in-flight runs**: A ref needed by a running workflow must never be deleted mid-run.\n23\t- **Terminal-only cleanup**: Only refs from completed runs are eligible; in-flight runs retain their refs.\n24\t\n25\t### The epoch prefix solution\n26\t\n27\tRef names carry their creation time in the epoch component:\n28\t\n29\t```\n30\trefs/gantry/1720441234-abc123def456...\n31\t           ^----epoch----^ ^----SHA----^\n32\t```\n33\t\n34\t**Epoch** = Unix timestamp (seconds) at push time.\n35\t\n36\tThis enables the opportunistic sweep (plan §4):\n37\t\n38\t1. The lease only matters for borderline cases near the sweep threshold.\n44\t\n45\t## The content-addressing tradeoff\n46\t\n47\t### What we lose\n48\t\n49\tThe same commit SHA pushed at time T₁ and again at time T₂ creates two refs:\n50\t\n51\t```\n52\trefs/gantry/1720441200-abc123... Identical content can exist under multiple ref names.\n57\t\n58\t### Why this is acceptable\n59\t\n60\t1. **Refs are cheap**: Git ref storage is minimal (~40 bytes per ref). Even at fleet scale (1000 runs/day, 7-day retention), this is ~280KB of ref storage — negligible compared to the repo size.\n61\t\n62\t2. **Refs are hidden**: `refs/gantry/*` never appear in `git branch` output and are not user-visible. They're implementation details, not branch names.\n63\t\n64\t3. **Refs are transient**: The epoch sweep deletes refs older than the retention window (typically 7 days). Duplication is bounded and short-lived.\n65\t\n66\t4. **No coordination needed**: Each box can safely sweep refs it created without consulting other boxes. A ref created by box A at epoch E₁ is never touched by box B's sweep — only box A sweeps it (when box A's next run happens to trigger the sweep).\n67\t\n68\t5. **Invariants preserved**: The critical invariant is \"no branch ref ever moves\" (INV-2). Epoch refs satisfy this: they're refs under `refs/gantry/*`, never `refs/heads/*`. Branch refs are untouched.\n69\t\n70\t## Alternatives considered\n71\t\n72\t### Alternative 1: Pure content addressing (`refs/gantry/<sha>`)\n73\t\n74\t- **Problem**: No epoch information means we can't implement \"delete refs older than N days\" without external metadata.\n75\t- **We'd need**: A separate timestamp store (file, database, git note) that maps sha → push time.\n76\t- **Why rejected**: External metadata is fragile (state drift, cross-box coordination, recovery after corruption). The epoch prefix carries the metadata *in the ref name itself*.\n77\t\n78\t### Alternative 2: Branch refs (`refs/heads/gantry/<sha>`)\n79\t\n80\t- **Problem**: Violates INV-2 (\"no branch ref ever moves\") and security consideration S-1 (\"no implicit branch pushes\").\n81\t- **Why rejected**: The predecessor's worst incident class was accidental branch pushes. Hidden refs under `refs/gantry/*` are safe; branch refs are not.\n82\t\n83\t### Alternative 3: Cross-box coordination via shared state\n84\t\n85\t- **Problem**: Requires a shared database or centralized GC service.\n86\t- **Why rejected**: Violates \"no daemon,\" adds operational complexity, creates a single point of failure. The epoch prefix is *fully distributed*.\n87\t\n88\t## Lease records (EC-09)\n89\t\n90\t### What is a lease?\n91\t\n92\tA lease is a client-side record that protects a ref while a run is in-flight:\n93\t\n94\t```json\n95\t{\n96\t  \"ref\": \"refs/gantry/1720441234-abc123...\",\n97\t  \"run_id\": \"01J...\",\n98\t  \"created_at\": 1720441234,\n99\t  \"expires_at\": 1720444834  // created_at + lease_duration (default 1 hour)\n100\t}\n101\t```\n102\t\n103\tStored in the state dir (`~/.local/state/gantry/leases.jsonl`), one record per push.\n104\t\n105\t### Why leases exist\n106\t\n107\tThe epoch sweep must never delete a ref that an in-flight run still needs. Leagues solve this:\n108\t\n109\t- When pushing: append a lease record with `expires_at = now + lease_duration`.\n110\t- When sweeping: *only* delete refs whose epoch is expired **AND** whose lease has expired.\n111\t- When a run finishes: mark its lease as \"terminal\" (the run ended, but the ref is kept for the retention window).\n112\t\n113\t### Cross-box independence (EC-09)\n114\t\n115\t**Lease records are local to each box.** Box A does not see Box B's leases, and vice versa. This is intentional:\n116\t\n117\t- Each box sweeps only refs it created (tracked via local lease records).\n118\t- A ref from Box A is never touched by Box B's sweep.\n119\t- No coordination needed: the `ls-remote` output is shared, but the *decision* to delete is local.\n120\t\n121\tThis means:\n122\t- If the same SHA is pushed by two boxes at different times, two refs exist. Each box GCs its own ref independently.\n123\t- No centralized state, no distributed consensus, no \"who owns this ref?\" ambiguity.\n124\t\n125\t### Lease expiry and retention\n126\t\n127\tTwo time bounds:\n128\t\n129\t1. **Lease duration** (default: 1 hour): How long a ref is protected while a run is in-flight. If a run takes longer than 1 hour, the lease is extended on-demand.\n130\t2. **Retention window** (default: 7 days): How long terminal refs are kept after the run completes.\n131\t\n132\tThe sweep deletes refs whose epoch is older than the retention window **AND** whose lease is expired. Terminal refs (run finished) are kept for the retention window, then deleted.\n133\t\n134\t## Sweep threshold calculation\n135\t\n136\tThe sweep operates on a time threshold derived from the retention window:\n137\t\n138\t```rust\n139\tlet now = epoch_now();\n140\tlet sweep_threshold = now - RETENTION_WINDOW_SECONDS;  // e.g., 7 days ago\n141\t\n142\t// Delete iff: epoch < sweep_threshold AND lease expired\n143\tfor ref in ls_remote(\"refs/gantry/*\") {\n144\t    let epoch = extract_epoch_from_ref_name(&ref);\n145\t    if epoch < sweep_threshold && lease_is_expired(&ref) {\n146\t        git push remote :<ref>;  // delete\n147\t    }\n148\t}\n149\t```\n150\t\n151\tThis ensures:\n152\t- Recent refs (epoch >= sweep_threshold) are never touched, regardless of lease state.\n153\t- Old refs (epoch < sweep_threshold) are deleted only if their lease is expired.\n154\t- In-flight runs retain their refs even if the epoch is old (lease is not expired).\n155\t\n156\t## Edge cases\n157\t\n158\t### EC-09: Same sha pushed by two boxes in the same epoch window\n159\t\n160\tIf two boxes push the same SHA within the same epoch window (e.g., within the same second), the ref names collide: both push `refs/gantry/1720441234-abc123...`.\n161\t\n162\t**Behavior**: The second push is a no-op (git push with the same ref SHA is idempotent). Both boxes record separate leases, but they refer to the same ref on the remote.\n163\t\n164\t**Cleanup**: When the first box sweeps this ref, it deletes it from the remote. The second box's lease now points to a deleted ref — but this is benign: the run is already terminal, so the ref is no longer needed. The second box's next sweep simply sees \"ref not found\" and continues.\n165\t\n166\t### Clock skew between boxes\n167\t\n168\tDifferent boxes may have slightly unsynchronized clocks (seconds-level skew). This is acceptable:\n169\t\n170\t- The retention window (7 days) is large compared to typical clock skew (<1s).\n171\t- A ref deleted \"too early\" by a fast-clock box is not a correctness issue: the run is terminal, so the ref is no longer needed.\n172\t- A ref deleted \"too late\" by a slow-clock box is also acceptable: it just means a few extra refs linger until the next sweep.\n173\t\n174\t### Shard-scoped refs vs. global refs\n175\t\n176\tThe design uses *local lease records*, which means each box GCs only its own refs. This is a tradeoff:\n177\t\n178\t- **Pro**: No coordination, simple, robust.\n179\t- **Con**: If box A dies and never sweeps again, its refs persist until another mechanism cleans them up (e.g., server-side ref expiration, if available).\n180\t\n181\t**Acceptance**: This is deemed acceptable for v1. The refs are hidden, cheap, and bounded (7-day retention). If a box dies, its refs age out naturally. A future v1.x enhancement could add a \"global sweep\" mode for clusters with a dedicated GC service.\n182\t\n183\t## Implementation plan (Phase 1a, bf-3v5)\n184\t\n185\t1. **RefPusher::push** enhancement:\n186\t   - Terminal runs marked `terminal: true` when verdict is recorded.\n195\t\n196\t3. **Sweep logic**:\n197\t   - Run `git ls-remote <ci_remote> \"refs/gantry/*\"` to list all refs.\n198\t   - Extract epoch from each ref name.\n199\t   - For each ref, check local lease state.\n200\t   - Delete iff `epoch < sweep_threshold` AND `lease.expired` AND (if `!terminal`, `lease.expires_at < now`).\n201\t   - Each box only sweeps refs it has leases for (EC-09).\n202\t\n203\t4. **Config**:\n204\t   - Add `push_mode` field (`\"ref\"` default, `\"branch\"` legacy with warning).\n205\t   - Add `lease_duration_seconds` (default 3600 = 1 hour).\n206\t   - Add `retention_days` (default 7).\n207\t\n208\t5. **Testing**:\n209\t   - Unit test for epoch extraction from ref name.\n210\t   - Unit test for sweep threshold calculation.\n211\t   - Integration test: push → lease created → sweep deletes old ref.\n212\t   - Integration test: same SHA, two epochs → two refs → both swept independently.\n213\t   - Property test: ref name fuzzing ensures epoch is always extractable.\n214\t\n215\t## Summary\n216\t\n217\t**Decision**: Epoch refs (`refs/gantry/<epoch>-<sha>`) are the chosen design.\n218\t\n219\t**Rationale**:\n220\t- Enables GC without daemon, coordination, or external metadata.\n221\t- Accepts content-addressing tradeoff (duplicate refs for same SHA) as cheap and harmless.\n222\t- Preserves critical invariants (no branch mutation, hidden refs).\n223\t- Lease records are local (EC-09), enabling fully distributed GC.\n224\t\n225\t**Alternatives rejected**: Pure content addressing (requires external metadata), branch refs (violates INV-2), cross-box coordination (violates \"no daemon\").\n226\t\n227\t**Phase 1a acceptance**: RefPusher with leases + opportunistic sweep, push failure → InfraFailure, `push_mode=branch` legacy support with warning.\n228\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"dcdc2b24-b137-487d-89f7-17554132f051","uuid":"a2ff321c-b333-4fc0-b9b2-dc7323f4027c","timestamp":"2026-07-28T18:13:06.326Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/coding/gantry-rs/docs/notes/epoch-refs-design.md","content":"# Epoch refs design note\n\n*Plan R2 resolution: epoch-vs-content-addressing tension (Q-3). Settled before Phase 1a RefPusher implementation (bf-3v5).*\n\n## The tension\n\nRefPusher creates hidden refs on a git remote to ship commits to the remote executor. The ref naming scheme carries two competing goals:\n\n1. **Content addressing**: The same commit SHA pushed at different times should resolve to a single ref, avoiding duplication.\n2. **Epoch-based GC**: Refs must carry enough metadata to enable garbage collection without a daemon or cross-box coordination.\n\nThe epoch-prefix scheme `refs/gantry/<epoch>-<sha>` resolves this tension in favor of *epoch-based GC*, accepting that identical SHAs may exist under multiple refs at different times.\n\n## Why epoch refs\n\n### Problem statement\n\nWe need a GC mechanism for `refs/gantry/*` that satisfies:\n\n- **No daemon**: No cron job, no background process (plan §4).\n- **No cross-box coordination**: Each gantry instance must operate independently (EC-09).\n- **No race with in-flight runs**: A ref needed by a running workflow must never be deleted mid-run.\n- **Terminal-only cleanup**: Only refs from completed runs are eligible; in-flight runs retain their refs.\n\n### The epoch prefix solution\n\nRef names carry their creation time in the epoch component:\n\n```\nrefs/gantry/1720441234-abc123def456...\n           ^----epoch----^ ^----SHA----^\n```\n\n**Epoch** = Unix timestamp (seconds) at push time.\n\nThis enables the opportunistic sweep (plan §4):\n\n1. Every successful push *also* queries `ls-remote` for all `refs/gantry/*` refs.\n2. For each ref: extract its epoch from the ref name.\n3. Delete iff `epoch < now_sweep_threshold` AND the local run record is terminal (pass/fail/gate_failure).\n4. Each box sweeps only refs it created (lease records are local; see EC-09).\n\nNo daemon, no coordination, no races: a ref whose epoch is \"recent enough\" is always kept, regardless of which box created it. The lease only matters for borderline cases near the sweep threshold.\n\n## The content-addressing tradeoff\n\n### What we lose\n\nThe same commit SHA pushed at time T₁ and again at time T₂ creates two refs:\n\n```\nrefs/gantry/1720441200-abc123...  (push #1)\nrefs/gantry/1720444800-abc123...  (push #2, same SHA, later epoch)\n```\n\nThis is *not* pure content addressing. Identical content can exist under multiple ref names.\n\n### Why this is acceptable\n\n1. **Refs are cheap**: Git ref storage is minimal (~40 bytes per ref). Even at fleet scale (1000 runs/day, 7-day retention), this is ~280KB of ref storage — negligible compared to the repo size.\n\n2. **Refs are hidden**: `refs/gantry/*` never appear in `git branch` output and are not user-visible. They're implementation details, not branch names.\n\n3. **Refs are transient**: The epoch sweep deletes refs older than the retention window (typically 7 days). Duplication is bounded and short-lived.\n\n4. **No coordination needed**: Each box can safely sweep refs it created without consulting other boxes. A ref created by box A at epoch E₁ is never touched by box B's sweep — only box A sweeps it (when box A's next run happens to trigger the sweep).\n\n5. **Invariants preserved**: The critical invariant is \"no branch ref ever moves\" (INV-2). Epoch refs satisfy this: they're refs under `refs/gantry/*`, never `refs/heads/*`. Branch refs are untouched.\n\n## Alternatives considered\n\n### Alternative 1: Pure content addressing (`refs/gantry/<sha>`)\n\n- **Problem**: No epoch information means we can't implement \"delete refs older than N days\" without external metadata.\n- **We'd need**: A separate timestamp store (file, database, git note) that maps sha → push time.\n- **Why rejected**: External metadata is fragile (state drift, cross-box coordination, recovery after corruption). The epoch prefix carries the metadata *in the ref name itself*.\n\n### Alternative 2: Branch refs (`refs/heads/gantry/<sha>`)\n\n- **Problem**: Violates INV-2 (\"no branch ref ever moves\") and security consideration S-1 (\"no implicit branch pushes\").\n- **Why rejected**: The predecessor's worst incident class was accidental branch pushes. Hidden refs under `refs/gantry/*` are safe; branch refs are not.\n\n### Alternative 3: Cross-box coordination via shared state\n\n- **Problem**: Requires a shared database or centralized GC service.\n- **Why rejected**: Violates \"no daemon,\" adds operational complexity, creates a single point of failure. The epoch prefix is *fully distributed*.\n\n## Lease records (EC-09)\n\n### What is a lease?\n\nA lease is a client-side record that protects a ref while a run is in-flight:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"ref\": \"refs/gantry/1720441234-abc123...\",\n  \"run_id\": \"01J...\",\n  \"created_at\": 1720441234,\n  \"expires_at\": 1720444834  // created_at + lease_duration (default 1 hour)\n}\n```\n\nStored in the state dir (`~/.local/state/gantry/leases.jsonl`), one record per push.\n\n### Why leases exist\n\nThe epoch sweep must never delete a ref that an in-flight run still needs. Leagues solve this:\n\n- When pushing: append a lease record with `expires_at = now + lease_duration`.\n- When sweeping: *only* delete refs whose epoch is expired **AND** whose lease has expired.\n- When a run finishes: mark its lease as \"terminal\" (the run ended, but the ref is kept for the retention window).\n\n### Cross-box independence (EC-09)\n\n**Lease records are local to each box.** Box A does not see Box B's leases, and vice versa. This is intentional:\n\n- Each box sweeps only refs it created (tracked via local lease records).\n- A ref from Box A is never touched by Box B's sweep.\n- No coordination needed: the `ls-remote` output is shared, but the *decision* to delete is local.\n\nThis means:\n- If the same SHA is pushed by two boxes at different times, two refs exist. Each box GCs its own ref independently.\n- No centralized state, no distributed consensus, no \"who owns this ref?\" ambiguity.\n\n### Lease expiry and retention\n\nTwo time bounds:\n\n1. **Lease duration** (default: 1 hour): How long a ref is protected while a run is in-flight. If a run takes longer than 1 hour, the lease is extended on-demand.\n2. **Retention window** (default: 7 days): How long terminal refs are kept after the run completes.\n\nThe sweep deletes refs whose epoch is older than the retention window **AND** whose lease is expired. Terminal refs (run finished) are kept for the retention window, then deleted.\n\n## Sweep threshold calculation\n\nThe sweep operates on a time threshold derived from the retention window:\n\n```rust\nlet now = epoch_now();\nlet sweep_threshold = now - RETENTION_WINDOW_SECONDS;  // e.g., 7 days ago\n\n// Delete iff: epoch < sweep_threshold AND lease expired\nfor ref in ls_remote(\"refs/gantry/*\") {\n    let epoch = extract_epoch_from_ref_name(&ref);\n    if epoch < sweep_threshold && lease_is_expired(&ref) {\n        git push remote :<ref>;  // delete\n    }\n}\n```\n\nThis ensures:\n- Recent refs (epoch >= sweep_threshold) are never touched, regardless of lease state.\n- Old refs (epoch < sweep_threshold) are deleted only if their lease is expired.\n- In-flight runs retain their refs even if the epoch is old (lease is not expired).\n\n## Edge cases\n\n### EC-09: Same sha pushed by two boxes in the same epoch window\n\nIf two boxes push the same SHA within the same epoch window (e.g., within the same second), the ref names collide: both push `refs/gantry/1720441234-abc123...`.\n\n**Behavior**: The second push is a no-op (git push with the same ref SHA is idempotent). Both boxes record separate leases, but they refer to the same ref on the remote.\n\n**Cleanup**: When the first box sweeps this ref, it deletes it from the remote. The second box's lease now points to a deleted ref — but this is benign: the run is already terminal, so the ref is no longer needed. The second box's next sweep simply sees \"ref not found\" and continues.\n\n### Clock skew between boxes\n\nDifferent boxes may have slightly unsynchronized clocks (seconds-level skew). This is acceptable:\n\n- The retention window (7 days) is large compared to typical clock skew (<1s).\n- A ref deleted \"too early\" by a fast-clock box is not a correctness issue: the run is terminal, so the ref is no longer needed.\n- A ref deleted \"too late\" by a slow-clock box is also acceptable: it just means a few extra refs linger until the next sweep.\n\n### Shard-scoped refs vs. global refs\n\nThe design uses *local lease records*, which means each box GCs only its own refs. This is a tradeoff:\n\n- **Pro**: No coordination, simple, robust.\n- **Con**: If box A dies and never sweeps again, its refs persist until another mechanism cleans them up (e.g., server-side ref expiration, if available).\n\n**Acceptance**: This is deemed acceptable for v1. The refs are hidden, cheap, and bounded (7-day retention). If a box dies, its refs age out naturally. A future v1.x enhancement could add a \"global sweep\" mode for clusters with a dedicated GC service.\n\n## Implementation plan (Phase 1a, bf-3v5)\n\n1. **RefPusher::push** enhancement:\n   - Add client-side lease record creation on push.\n   - Add opportunistic sweep after successful push.\n   - Add `push_mode = \"branch\"` legacy support with warning.\n   - Map push failures to `InfraFailure` (plan §4).\n\n2. **Lease storage**:\n   - Append-only JSONL file in state dir (`~/.local/state/gantry/leases.jsonl`).\n   - One record per push: `{\"ref\": \"...\", \"run_id\": \"...\", \"created_at\": ..., \"expires_at\": ..., \"terminal\": false}`.\n   - Terminal runs marked `terminal: true` when verdict is recorded.\n\n3. **Sweep logic**:\n   - Run `git ls-remote <ci_remote> \"refs/gantry/*\"` to list all refs.\n   - Extract epoch from each ref name.\n   - For each ref, check local lease state.\n   - Delete iff `epoch < sweep_threshold` AND `lease.expired` AND (if `!terminal`, `lease.expires_at < now`).\n   - Each box only sweeps refs it has leases for (EC-09).\n\n4. **Config**:\n   - Add `push_mode` field (`\"ref\"` default, `\"branch\"` legacy with warning).\n   - Add `lease_duration_seconds` (default 3600 = 1 hour).\n   - Add `retention_days` (default 7).\n\n5. **Testing**:\n   - Unit test for epoch extraction from ref name.\n   - Unit test for sweep threshold calculation.\n   - Integration test: push → lease created → sweep deletes old ref.\n   - Integration test: same SHA, two epochs → two refs → both swept independently.\n   - Property test: ref name fuzzing ensures epoch is always extractable.\n\n## Summary\n\n**Decision**: Epoch refs (`refs/gantry/<epoch>-<sha>`) are the chosen design.\n\n**Rationale**:\n- Enables GC without daemon, coordination, or external metadata.\n- Accepts content-addressing tradeoff (duplicate refs for same SHA) as cheap and harmless.\n- Preserves critical invariants (no branch mutation, hidden refs).\n- Lease records are local (EC-09), enabling fully distributed GC.\n\n**Alternatives rejected**: Pure content addressing (requires external metadata), branch refs (violates INV-2), cross-box coordination (violates \"no daemon\").\n\n**Phase 1a acceptance**: RefPusher with leases + opportunistic sweep, push failure → InfraFailure, `push_mode=branch` legacy support with warning.\n","numLines":228,"startLine":1,"totalLines":228}}}
